bull.b: Expansion among large enterprise customers supports durable recurring-revenue growth and demonstrates increasing platform relevance. More high-value accounts also create a broader base for cross-selling Zero Trust, data security, AI security and other modules over multiple contract cycles.

Strong operating and free cash flow provides financial flexibility despite reported accounting losses. Consistent positive cash generation can fund product development, infrastructure investment and go-to-market expansion while reducing reliance on external financing.

Growing demand for AI security adds a structural product category to Zscaler’s existing zero-trust platform. This can increase wallet share with current customers, support new use cases and diversify growth beyond traditional seat-based subscriptions.

bear.b: Persistent GAAP operating and net losses show that the business has not yet fully converted scale and gross-margin strength into bottom-line profitability. Continued losses can constrain capital allocation flexibility and leave execution dependent on sustaining the improvement trajectory.

The expected deceleration indicates that the company must sustain a larger revenue base while growth normalizes from an exceptionally strong prior year. Slower expansion could reduce operating leverage and increase the importance of successful platform upselling and new product adoption.

Higher infrastructure costs for memory, storage, processors and appliances can pressure free-cash-flow conversion as Zscaler scales its cloud platform. Sustained investment may be strategically necessary, but it raises execution demands and limits near-term cash operating leverage.
